notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Isaiah 23 this time, because I wasn't able to read a single source page.

When I tried to load the commentary pages (Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary, Barnes and Calvin on BibleHub, Precept Austin, and the NET Bible notes), the tool returned a usage-limit error. A second try at just Enduring Word was also blocked because I had used up my allowed tool calls. Your rules say to report only what the pages I read actually say, never fill gaps from my own knowledge, and give a URL for every point. With nothing read, any notes would come from memory, so I've left them out.

If you ask again in a new turn, I'll start with one source at a time instead of loading several at once, which is probably what triggered the limit. I'd go in this order:
1. **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary and Barnes on BibleHub, and Precept Austin.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Calvin and Wesley's notes, and Spurgeon, Ligonier or Got Questions if they cover this chapter. The verses most likely to show differences are vv. 15–18: what the seventy years refer to, and how Tyre's earnings could be "set apart to the LORD."
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes, which are useful for hard spots like v. 13 ("land of the Chaldeans") and v. 10, and Catholic or Orthodox sources if they have anything on this chapter.

If you'd like a smaller first batch, I could cover just Enduring Word and Ellicott first and add the rest in later turns.
